description: Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.

a.request: Using only fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is greater than 0.0005, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, provided that overall mean is not missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Return the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and this relative ratio for the 10 orders with the highest relative ratio, sorted from highest to lowest with missing values last.
a.sql:
WITH per_order AS (
  SELECT orderslink,
         AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal,
         AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
stats AS (
  SELECT orderslink, avg_rebtotal, avg_ratio,
         AVG(avg_ratio) OVER () AS mean_ratio
  FROM per_order
)
SELECT orderslink AS order_link,
       avg_rebtotal,
       avg_ratio,
       avg_ratio / NULLIF(mean_ratio, 0) AS relative_ratio
FROM stats
ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

d.request: For fee records with `rebrate > 0.0005` (strictly greater), group by `orderslink`, compute each order's average `rebtotal` and average of `rebrate / feerate` (skipping NULLs), divide each order's average ratio by the mean of those averages across all orders (when that mean is not NULL), and return the top 10 orders by relative ratio, descending, NULLs last.
d.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), stats AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_avg_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio / NULLIF(s.mean_avg_ratio, 0) AS relative_ratio FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN stats s ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

c.request: For fee records that clear the 0.0005 maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) threshold, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, as long as that overall mean isn't missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Show the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and the relative ratio for the top 10 orders by relative ratio, highest first, with missing values last. Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.
c.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT orderslink, rebtotal, rebrate, feerate
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
),
per_order AS (
  SELECT orderslink,
         AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal,
         AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order
)
SELECT p.orderslink,
       p.avg_rebtotal,
       p.avg_ratio,
       CASE WHEN o.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL AND o.mean_ratio <> 0
            THEN p.avg_ratio / o.mean_ratio
       END AS relative_ratio
FROM per_order p
CROSS JOIN overall o
ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

b.request: Group fee records where `rebrate > 0.0005` by `orderslink`, compute per-order AVG(`rebtotal`) and AVG(`rebrate` / `feerate`) ignoring NULLs, normalize each order's average ratio by the mean of those per-order averages, and return the top 10 orders by relative ratio descending with NULLs last.
b.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_rebate_fee_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), normalized AS (SELECT orderslink, avg_rebtotal, avg_rebate_fee_ratio, avg_rebate_fee_ratio / NULLIF(AVG(avg_rebate_fee_ratio) OVER (), 0) AS relative_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT orderslink, avg_rebtotal, avg_rebate_fee_ratio, relative_ratio FROM normalized ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
